incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: High error rate detected for ingress ALB in euc2a (502/connection-reset spike). Auto-alerting oncall.
elena: I'm paged, looking now. seeing 502 spike from ALB target group -> envoy upstream resets.
raj: grabbing logs from envoy pods in euc2a, tailing envoy access: `kubectl -n infra logs -l app=envoy --since=5m`
kevin: I'll pull ALB metrics (ELB console + cloudwatch). suspecting keepalive idle mismatch after the last config roll earlier today.
nicole: customers reporting upload failures, support-ops flagged a few paying customers losing requests (uploads time out then 502). can we estimate impact?
support-ops: ~1.8% of requests failing in euc2a over last 10m, errors concentrated on multipart upload endpoints. Customer-facing dashboard shows increased 5xx.
elena: Rolling repro steps: curl through ALB to a known backend, observe `Connection reset by peer` intermittently.
raj: Paste of envoy log snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T12:34:05Z] upstream reset: connection failure, error: ECONNRESET
[2026-03-15T12:34:06Z] downstream conn closed: client reused closed socket
```
kevin: ALB target-group attributes show `deregistration_delay` still default. Also `idle_timeout` was changed to 60s earlier today while Envoy expects 300s. mismatch leads to ALB closing idle connections; clients reuse socket -> envoy sees reset.
elena: that explains the resets. Quick mitigation idea: set ALB `idle_timeout` back to 300s, or flip ALB to close keepalives (disable keepalive) until we roll envoy fix. Which is faster?
kevin: Changing ALB attribute is fast but will take a few propagation minutes across AZs. Disabling keepalive at ALB would force new connections per request — it's risky for latency.
raj: We can temporarily shift traffic away from euc2a to euc2b/c via Route53 weighted records as a short circuit while we fix config. That buys time without double load on others?
nicole: Agree. If we weight euc2a down to 5% and push traffic to healthy AZs, customers should see fewer failures. Do we have capacity headroom?
support-ops: euc2b/c current CPU/GPU headroom is ~30% at baseline, should absorb short-term traffic shift.
elena: OK I'll start traffic shift. tagging @kevin to update ALB idle_timeout concurrently.
kevin: Running modify-target-group-attributes for the ALB to set `idle_timeout.timeout_seconds=300` now:
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:... --attributes Key=idle_timeout.timeout_seconds,Value=300
```
incident-bot: :information_source: Action logged: modify-target-group-attributes by kevin.
raj: While idle_timeout propagates, starting Route53 weighted routing change via infra runbook: `route53 set-weight euc2a=5 euc2b=47 euc2c=48` (dry run then apply).
elena: Command executed, lowering euc2a weight to 5%.
support-ops: Monitoring dashboard — 5xx rate in euc2a dropped by 75% in the next 60s. Overall customer 5xx decreased ~1.3 percentage points.
kevin: ALB attribute update returned success. Propagation across ALB nodes may still take ~90s.
raj: I'm also bouncing a small set of envoy pods with a patched config to tolerate early resets (defensive), `kubectl rollout restart deploy/envoy -n infra --selector=canary=true` — canary in euc2b first.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for envoy (tag=canary-reset-tolerance).
nicole: Any sign of conntrack / socket table exhaustion? That could make symptoms worse.
raj: Checked node metrics — conntrack close to normal. Not a conntrack exhaustion event. This is primarily idle keepalive mismatch.
elena: Good. Next: plan for a full rollback of today's change to ALB idle_timeout in the deploy PR to keep values consistent until we update envoy to the new behavior.
kevin: I'll open PR to revert the ALB idle_timeout change in infra repo and attach rollback plan.
support-ops: Noting customers affected and contacting top 5 with ETA: mitigation applied, traffic shifted, expecting resolution within 30m.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident severity set to SEV2 due to customer impact and partial service degradation. Paging escalation on.
elena: Post-mitigation checklist: 1) Keep routing weights reduced for 20m 2) Confirm ALB idle_timeout stable 3) Roll envoy fix cluster-wide with controlled ramp 4) Postmortem
raj: Envoy can be updated to detect upstream FIN and avoid reusing a closed socket, plus add healthcheck tuning. I'll prepare the fix for today's release train.
kevin: ALB attributes now stable, Amazon reports attribute sync complete.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout completed with no regression metrics. Starting gradual rollout to 50% then 100% per runbook.
elena: Gradual rollout to 100% started. Monitoring for errors — if errors climb, rollback.
support-ops: Customer notes: error rates back to baseline for most. A couple of long-tail client retries still failing; they are on old SDKs that aggressively reuse connections. Recommending client-side SDK update in postmortem.
nicole: We'll draft outbound comms to affected customers explaining cause: keepalive timeout mismatch between ALB and Envoy after config change; mitigation: traffic shift, ALB timeout revert, envoy fix. ETA for customer email: 2 hours.
incident-bot: Incident marked as "mitigated" — services stable in all AZs; monitoring in watch for 60 minutes.
elena: Turning incident to follow-up. Oncall handoff to raj for postmortem and root cause. Raj, you're owning the postmortem, add timeline and remediation actions.
raj: On it. Immediate actions: 1) Reconcile infra change control to include cross-check of keepalive values 2) Add test that asserts ALB and Envoy idle_timeout parity in infra CI 3) Recommend SDK guidance for clients.
kevin: I'll include ALB attribute verification in deploy gating.
nicole: I'll prepare customer comms draft and coordinate with support-ops.
support-ops: Stand down — monitoring continuing. Thanks team. :heart:
__meta: generated by dataset-gen: unique incident thread about ALB keepalive mismatch and rapid mitigation via Route53 weighting
